summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 20%), COPD, type 2 diabetes, and polysubstance use was admitted for acute shortness of breath after missing medications and using crack cocaine. He presented with tachypnea, hypoxia, and signs of fluid overload. Imaging showed worsening bilateral lung opacities, and he was treated for both possible pneumonia and chemical pneumonitis from crack inhalation. He received a course of antibiotics and a short steroid regimen for lung inflammation, with gradual improvement in oxygenation. Acute kidney injury developed due to over-diuresis but resolved with fluid management. His diuretic was adjusted to 30mg torsemide, metoprolol was held due to cocaine use, and he was discharged home on a prednisone taper with follow-up plans. Social work addressed his housing instability and substance use.
